section_summary: This section contains U.S. State Department records from May and June 1948 concerning Japanese economic rehabilitation, regional conditions, and post-war planning. It includes a critical telegram from Manila regarding War Department unilateralism, an extensive survey report by David M. Bane covering economic, labor, and communist activity across northern Honshu and Hokkaido, and the transmittal of the Japanese Economic Stabilization Board's draft five-year rehabilitation plan. The draft plan sets comprehensive production, trade, power, and consumption goals designed to restore Japan to 1930–1934 living standards by 1952.

subfiles.about: The telegram criticizes a War Department commission report recommending unilateral American action on Japanese economic policy in defiance of the Far Eastern Commission.
subfiles.summary: Telegram from Manila arguing that a War Department report arbitrarily urges unilateral action on Japan defying other Far Eastern Commission nations.
subfiles.title: Telegram No. 226 from Manila regarding War Department Policy on Japan

subfiles.about: Cover despatch transmitting Foreign Service Officer David M. Bane's report on his survey trip through northern Honshu and Hokkaido.
subfiles.summary: Transmittal despatch enclosing David M. Bane's survey report on economic and political conditions in northern Japan.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 307: Transmission of Report of Survey Trip through Northern Japan

subfiles.about: David M. Bane details his firsthand observations of economic resources, industrial development, labor unrest, communist activity, and transportation in northern Honshu and Hokkaido.
subfiles.summary: David M. Bane reports on his survey of Niigata, Akita, Aomori, Hokkaido, and Miyagi, assessing natural resources including oil, coal, and natural gas. He evaluates industrial output, transportation bottlenecks, black markets, and the progress of agrarian land reform and cooperatives. The report highlights management intimidation, significant communist infiltration within labor and teachers' unions, and regional reliance on American occupation authorities.
subfiles.title: Report of Survey Trip Taken by David M. Bane, Second Secretary of Mission, to Points in Northern Honshu and Hokkaido During the Period May 5 to May 12, 1948

subfiles.about: Despatch transmitting the Economic Stabilization Board's draft five-year plan for Japanese economic rehabilitation along with Japanese press commentary and committee regulations.
subfiles.summary: Despatch enclosing the Economic Stabilization Board's draft five-year recovery plan and summarizing Japanese press reactions, including criticisms of feasibility, population assumptions, and committee composition.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 326: Japanese Economic Rehabilitation Plan

subfiles.about: A comprehensive five-year draft plan by the Economic Stabilization Board setting targets for Japanese production, trade, energy, food, and living standards from 1948 to 1952.
subfiles.summary: The Economic Stabilization Board outlines a five-year economic rehabilitation plan aiming to restore Japan's living standards and per-capita income close to 1930–1934 levels by 1952. It details projections and capital allocation priorities for coal, electric power, fertilizers, iron and steel, textiles, agriculture, and shipping reconstruction. The program underscores the imperative of controlling inflation, boosting labor productivity, expanding exports tenfold in machinery, and securing substantial foreign economic aid.
subfiles.title: Outline of Japanese Economy Rehabilitation Plan (1st Draft)
